description: Small human-labeled calibration set for the LLM-as-judge. Each answer was labeled L1-L5 by the rubric author against the competency's level anchors in competency_map.json. Includes good/bad answers to the same competency so discrimination is directly measurable.

samples.answer: For 500 calls I use asyncio.gather behind a semaphore to cap concurrency, wrap each call in a retry with exponential backoff and jitter, set a per-request timeout, and return partial results so one failure doesn't sink the batch.
samples.note: async + concurrency limits + backoff + timeouts = L4 anchor

samples.answer: I'd loop over the list and call the API one at a time in a normal for loop, with a try/except around it.
samples.note: synchronous loop, basic try/except = L2 anchor

samples.answer: I use the provider's structured-output / JSON-schema mode with a Pydantic model, validate on parse, and if validation fails I retry feeding the error back. I never regex free text.
samples.note: schema mode + validation + retry = L4

samples.answer: I put 'return JSON' in the prompt and then json.loads the response. Usually it works.
samples.note: parses free text and hopes = L2 anchor

samples.answer: I choose per requirements: pgvector when we already run Postgres and volume is modest, Qdrant when I need rich payload filtering at scale. I design metadata filters up front and pick HNSW vs IVF by the recall/latency trade-off.
samples.note: per-requirement choice + metadata + index trade-offs = L4

samples.answer: I've heard of Pinecone. I haven't really set one up, but I think it stores the vectors somewhere.
samples.note: knows the term, no real use = L1

samples.answer: I treat retrieved and user-supplied content as untrusted, keep instructions and data in separate channels, constrain tool permissions with allow-lists, and red-team with known injection payloads before shipping.
samples.note: untrusted content + isolation + limited tool perms = L4

samples.answer: I haven't really thought about it. The documents come from our own users so I trust them.
samples.note: trusts inputs = L1

samples.answer: I build a labeled query-to-relevant-doc set and track recall@k, precision, and MRR. I separate retrieval failures from generation failures, and use RAGAS for context precision and faithfulness.
samples.note: labeled set + recall/precision + separates failure types = L4

samples.answer: Structure-aware chunking on clause and section boundaries for contracts, overlap tuned to the embedding window, metadata per chunk. Chunking drives recall so I test it against a labeled set rather than guess.
samples.note: structure-aware + overlap reasoning + measured = L4

samples.answer: I route by task: a small fast model for classification and routing, a stronger model for scoring. I benchmark quality vs latency vs cost per 1k tokens and set per-task defaults with fallbacks.
samples.note: routes by quality/latency/cost with fallbacks = L4

samples.answer: I just use GPT-4 for everything since it's the strongest model.
samples.note: one model for everything = L2 anchor

samples.answer: I ask the model 'is this answer good, yes or no?' and go with what it says.
samples.note: asks 'is this good' = L2 anchor

samples.answer: If the model isn't good enough I'd fine-tune it on more of our data.
samples.note: fine-tuning as the default fix = L2 anchor

samples.answer: I add a line to the system prompt telling it not to hallucinate.
samples.note: 'don't hallucinate' = L2 anchor

samples.answer: My agent runs a ReAct loop; I cap it at a max number of steps and add a termination check so it can't spin forever. It's been running our support bot in production.
samples.note: ships with step limits and termination = L3

samples.answer: I serve it with FastAPI and stream tokens over SSE so the UI feels responsive, and I handle client disconnects.
samples.note: streams over SSE, handles disconnect, real project = L3

samples.answer: I keep a fixed test set and re-run it whenever I change a prompt, comparing outputs to catch regressions before I ship.
samples.note: fixed set re-run on change = L3 (not yet automated in CI)

samples.answer: I write structured system prompts that separate role, constraints, and tool descriptions, and I keep them versioned with the code.
samples.note: structured + versioned = L3

samples.answer: The context window is like how much text it can take. I'm not sure what happens if you go over, maybe it errors?
samples.note: vague, no real understanding = L1

samples.answer: I model agents as explicit typed state graphs, use subgraphs for modular assess/score stages, a Postgres checkpointer for resumability and human-in-the-loop interrupts, and I wrote our team's guide on when to use conditional edges vs tool calls.
samples.note: designs it + sets team patterns + mentors = L5

samples.answer: I treat a tool schema as a contract: precise descriptions, validated args, typed errors the model can recover from. I set our conventions for tool design and review the tools other engineers write.
samples.note: contract-level design + sets conventions + reviews others = L5
